svg.title: Audiobook Boss change map after contract, state, and tooling tightening
svg.desc: A before-versus-now diagram showing how Audiobook Boss changed after recent state-shape, runtime boundary, terminal progress, and release-tooling tightening work, plus the practical impact of those changes.
svg.text: Audiobook Boss: what changed since the previous repo-state map
This replaces the old snapshot with a delta view: what was tightened, what stayed the same, and why the new shape is more truthful and lower-drift.
What did not change
Runtime spine still holds
UI -> typed TS adapter -> Tauri IPC -> Rust owners remains the main reading order.
Wire events are still the same public channels
processing-progress
and
processing-queue
The work was mostly shape-tightening, not feature expansion
The app behaves the same from the outside, but internal truthfulness and anti-drift guarantees improved.
Before -> now -> practical effect
PREVIOUS MAP IMPLIED
CURRENT REPO STATE
WHY IT MATTERS
1. Status and file-list state were looser
Queued work could be excluded from aggregate percentage math.
Cover-art lookup could guess by basename and hit the wrong file.
Fresh imports could inherit stale file selection state.
The old system map named the UI seam, but not these truthfulness gaps inside it.
Status panel and file list now tell the truth more directly
Queued jobs count as 0%-complete participants in aggregate progress.
Thumbnail lookup prefers input index, then exact path, then unique basename only.
Fresh file-list replacement resets selection instead of carrying old indexes forward.
src/ui/statusPanel/state.ts, controller.ts, services/fileLookup.ts, src/ui/fileList/state.svelte.ts
Impact
Mixed queued/completed batches no longer report misleadingly high progress.
Art thumbnails stop hopping to the wrong row when filenames collide.
A fresh import starts from a clean local selection state.
2. The TS runtime boundary still carried extra drift room
The old map showed a typed boundary, but the client still concentrated casts.
There were two public metadata-save entry points for one command.
Event commentary and one runtime guard still reflected older migration history.
The previous diagram also named
save_metadata_to_file
as if it were still the main public story.
The TS boundary is narrower and more explicit now
Typed command specs and typed event normalizers replaced the broadest client casts.
Only
saveMetadataIntentToFile
remains as the public metadata-save entry point.
Dead event-guard/commentary cleanup brought docs closer to the live runtime path.
src/lib/tauri/client.ts, src/types/events.ts, src/lib/tauri-client.test.ts
Impact
Future IPC and event drift surfaces earlier in TypeScript instead of hiding behind casts.
There is one clear UI save path for metadata intent instead of a duplicated alias.
The boundary description is now closer to what actually runs.
3. Terminal progress emission had split paths
Cancellation already had a special path; failed terminal emission was still partly hand-built.
Batch failure results could lose job identity on some terminal paths.
Mixed cancelled-plus-failed batches were easier to blur into a cancellation-only story.
The old map gestured at terminalization, but not at these attribution details.
Terminal progress now has one clearer backend story
A centralized terminal-event helper emits failed and cancelled progress with shared shape.
Failed terminal results preserve
job_id
whenever that job had already been registered.
Cancellation stays truthful without masking real failures in mixed batch outcomes.
src-tauri/src/audio/progress/emitter.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/audio_processing.rs
Impact
The UI can correlate failures to the right job more reliably.
Cancel and fail terminal events are less likely to drift apart over time.
A mixed batch still leaves visible evidence when something truly failed.
4. Release/tooling/docs carried quiet maintenance drag
Release preview used
git log | head -15
under
pipefail
and the regression test ran too hot.
Release helper logic and context-surface lists were duplicated in shell scripts.
Recent changelog entries had drifted toward internal implementation detail.
Tooling/docs are more stable and lower-churn now
Release preview uses
git log --max-count=15
and the regression test fixture is cheaper plus timeout-safe.
Shared release helpers and deduped context-surface lists reduce script drift.
The changelog now reads more like release notes than an internal patch log.
Impact
Standard checks stay trustworthy on slower or colder machines.
Release scripts and anti-drift docs have fewer duplicated facts to keep aligned.
Future repo narration gets cheaper to maintain.
Bottom line

Relative to the old diagram, the biggest change is not a new subsystem. It is a tighter promise: status, events, client glue, and release tooling now guess less, preserve more truth, and leave less room for contract drift.
WHY REPLACE THE OLD MAP
The prior SVG and PNG still described a real architecture,
but they under-described the recent tightening work and
still pointed at stale details like the old metadata-save story.
Use this file as the current visual reference.

Repo-grounded sources: docs/api-map.md, docs/fallbacks.md, src/ui/statusPanel/state.ts, src/ui/statusPanel/controller.ts, src/ui/statusPanel/services/fileLookup.ts, src/ui/fileList/state.svelte.ts, src/lib/tauri/client.ts, src/types/events.ts, src-tauri/src/audio/progress/emitter.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/audio_processing.rs, scripts/release.sh, scripts/release.test.ts, scripts/lib/release-common.sh.
